findings.title: Validation has a DB-write side effect, so match_count is over-counted
findings.body: `should_block?` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at` and saves the record. It is called from `EmailValidator#validate_each`, which runs on every validation of a user whose email changed. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again. A single signup attempt with a blocked email therefore bumps the counter twice. Any other `valid?` call on a new or changed user does the same. Statistics collection and validation should be separate. Record the hit only when the block actually rejects a save, or do it explicitly in the controller.

findings.title: Read-modify-write counter update loses concurrent increments
findings.body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` is a read-modify-write on an in-memory copy. Two concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked address can both read N and both write N+1, losing a count. `save` also runs the model validations, including the uniqueness query, on every hit. An atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.increment_counter` or `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?")` avoids both problems.

findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so it can be bypassed
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact, case-sensitive match. Email addresses are case-insensitive, and the rest of the app normalizes with `Email.downcase`. A blocked address like `bad@spammers.org` can be bypassed by registering `Bad@Spammers.org`. The `uniqueness: true` validation and the unique index on `blocked_emails.email` are also case-sensitive, so case-variant duplicates can be stored. Normalize to lowercase on save and on lookup, or compare with `lower(email)`.

findings.title: Block check is skipped whenever any earlier error exists on the attribute
findings.body: The blocked-email check only runs if `record.errors[attribute].blank?`. Presence and uniqueness validators run first, so a duplicate email never reaches the check. Hit statistics for a blocked address are skipped whenever another error is present. The condition also depends on validator declaration order, which is fragile. Make the block check independent of other errors, or document that it is intentionally conditional.

findings.title: Every server-side email error is shown as a generic 'invalid' email
findings.body: On any failed signup where `result.errors.email` is present, the submitted email is added to `rejectedEmails`. `emailValidation` then shows `user.email.invalid` for that address. The server error may be that the email is already taken, is not allowed from that provider, or is blocked. All of these now show the same generic message, which can mislead the user. The list is also never cleared and is declared as `Em.A([])` on the controller prototype, so it is shared state.

findings.title: Moved whitelist/blacklist logic and the double-validation side effect are not tested
findings.body: The whitelist/blacklist domain logic moved from `User#email_validator` into `EmailValidator`, but the new validator spec only covers the blocked-email stub. No test covers the whitelist or blacklist branches, or the skip-when-already-errored behavior. Nothing checks that a signup with a blocked email returns the new `errors`/`values` fields from `UsersController#create`. Nothing covers case variants of a blocked address, and no test exposes that validating twice increments `match_count` twice.
